title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-28
content:
Daily scratchpad - GPU ops / capacity / network notes

2026-03-03 (Tue) - quick log and TODOs

Top priorities:
- Finalize spare GPU allocation plan for Dedicated cluster (zone-a) before EOD Thu. Target: reserve 10% of active pool (~8 A100s) for burst and canary jobs. Confirm with finance for cost delta. (JIRA: INFRA-542)
- Investigate 3x node disconnects in cluster-gpu-02 between 02:10-02:45 UTC. Suspect temporary NIC flaps after kernel patch. Need to reproduce and decide rollback window. (INFRA-559)
- Rolling maintenance Weds 03/04 01:00-03:00 UTC: NVLink firmware update on gpus in zone-b. Prep playbook + fallback (auto-fail to zone-a). Post-up checks list below.

Quick notes / findings:
- Observed larger tail latency on long-seq requests (seq>4096) starting ~03/01. Preliminary profiling: KV cache miss rate spiked for batches from model-prod routes. Might be due to cache eviction policy change on 02/28. Revert test planned on staging.
- Kernel 5.15.87-rt introduced new driver handling for Mellanox: mxnet/nic driver version mismatch? Check with infra-builder.
- Metrics: cluster-gpu-02 avg util 72% last 24h, p95 latency +18ms. cluster-gpu-01 steady at 65%.

Playbook checklist for maintenance (03/04):
- Pre-step (today): notify stakeholders (#infra-alerts + email to platform-eng + product-hosted-api).
- Backup: snapshot model volumes for affected nodes. Verify snapshots complete.
- Drain: cordon nodes, drain running inference pods, wait for traffic shift (monitor p95 and dropped requests).
- Apply NVLink firmware update. Run driver reload.
- Smoke tests: run small gen + embedding workload (2-3k tokens each) across affected nodes. Check kv-cache warmup and latency.
- Rollback: if >5% error increase or p95 latency regresses by >30ms after 30m, revert firmware and drivers, bring nodes back.
- Post: uncordon nodes, run post-update health check script (scripts/gpu/health-check.sh).

Commands / snippets to run during incident:
- Check NIC flaps: sudo journalctl -u systemd-networkd --since "2026-03-01" | grep -i mtu
- GPU driver version: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,gpu_name --format=csv
- KV cache stats (internal): curl -sS http://metrics-token:9100/kv-cache | jq '.' | grep "miss_rate"
- Kubernetes drain: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- [ ] Confirm spare GPU count with capacity planning spreadsheet and update Dedicated pricing estimate (talk to Ben in finance).
- [ ] Reproduce node disconnects on staging: coordinate with SRE to run stress-NIC tests on same kernel/driver combo. (Ethan to run test by Wed morning)
- [ ] Add automated alert for KV cache miss rate crossing 4% for >10m. (Linked alert rule draft in Alerting repo)
- [ ] Update runbook section on firmware updates with explicit rollback thresholds and Slack playbook templates.

Notes to self (short):
- If we need to fall back during maintenance, trigger policy: route traffic -> zone-a (capacity headroom ~18% currently) then scale up burst pool (uses reserved GPUs first).
- Remember to tag snapshots with tfvars deployment id to simplify cleanup.
- Ask research: can quantized model variant be used temporarily to reduce load during maintenance? Quick perf check required.

Meeting notes (standup 03/03):
- Jenna: working on autoscaler tuning (thresholds adjusted to p95 CPU 60% -> 55% for low-latency routes).
- Ethan: will run NIC stress test on staging today; suspects firmware/driver mismatch.
- Samir: prepping canary route and firmware playbook; will own rollback decision during window.

Useful links / refs:
- Capacity spreadsheet: https://sheets.redwood.example/d/1CapacityPlan
- Runbook (draft): https://confluence.redwood.example/ops/gpu-ops#firmware-updates
- Alerts: https://grafana.redwood.example/alerts/kv-cache-miss

End of page.

(Short, messy notes — clean up into runbook after maintenance.)
